xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF for GitHub issue #3932 (design-critique table-resolution precedence; bound by the arc, not by the issue body's proposed remedy)

plan.title: fix(design-critique): a typed verified-claims-table claim decides table resolution and cannot be masked by a generic citation

narratives.Description: `verdictForSynthesis` resolves the verified-claims table by scanning every citation for the first table-shaped body and never checks that citation's kind. A synthesis citing a table id that is not a table still clears, as long as some other cited comment happens to be table-shaped, because the `missing-table-cite` refusal only runs after the untyped search fails. This scope makes a typed table claim decide resolution, and keeps generic resolution for records that carry no typed claim.
narratives.Overview:
## Bound design

The issue body's proposed remedy was refuted by its own design-critique arc. Load-bearing artifacts: critic 5466473810, accepted successor lean 5466508563, verified-claims table 5466508630, synthesis 5466510155. The diagnosis survives; the remedy is replaced.

**Refuted -- not built here.** A blanket "only accept a `table`-kind citation" rule. Permalink citations are not typed: `verified-claims table <id>` scans as kind `table`, but `comment <id>`, `#issuecomment-<id>`, and `/issues/comments/<id>` all scan as kind `comment`. The repository locks `completed-arc-record.test.ts :: "completes a permalink synthesis, the form this arc's own record used"`, so a typed-only rule either silently clears with a null table or falsely refuses a published, tested form.

**Bound instead: a precedence rule in resolution.** When a typed table claim is present, resolution MUST be satisfied by that claim and MUST NOT be masked by generic citations. When no typed claim is present, today's generic permalink resolution stands. Narrowing the citation contract itself is a separate decision that would need its own migration criteria, and is not taken here.

**Cardinality -- chosen rule.** Every table-kind claim must resolve to the same verified-claims table artifact. The measured hole in the issue's own acceptance criteria is that one valid typed claim launders any number of invalid ones: with two typed claims, one real and one bogus, an implementation that filters to typed citations and takes the first table-shaped body finds the real one and never notices the ghost. Under the chosen rule every typed claim is examined, so a ghost alongside a real claim is refused in either order. `scanCitations` deduplicates on `(id, kind)`, so naming the same table id twice is still one claim; two distinct typed ids are two claims and cannot both be the record's table.

**Struck by the arc -- not built here.**

- Any `role:`-aware control. The evaluator sees only comment id and body, so any comment can self-label `role: parent`; body-declared role awareness would look deterministic while preserving the hazard.
- The successor-lean discovery direction (the false-refusal side). It stays on #3929. Both directions share the pattern "artifact identity inferred from role-blind body shape" but they are different predicates over different input sets and need separate fixes.

## File ownership

This scope owns `verdictForSynthesis` and the table-resolution path in `packages/core/src/design-critique/completed-arc-record.ts`. `content/contracts/design-critique.md` is owned by the parallel #3929 scope and is not edited here. The citation grammar and the position predicate are not widened.

Refs #3932, #3929, #3831, #3806, #3156.

Full task check is recorded by merged PR https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3950 squash ba3d6a8f; it is not re-run from scope:complete because FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES starts with verify:ac and would recurse.
narratives.Decisions: Cardinality rule: every table-kind claim must resolve to the same verified-claims table artifact (recorded in the code comment on the resolver and in the PR body).
